key_insight: Physics is most effective when learned once during training, with inference-time corrections reserved for residual geometric issues that the generator cannot easily represent.
engineering_relevance: For molecular crystal generation, post-training with physical signals improves validity and packing without slowing deployment, while runtime relaxation can fix clashes but incurs a large speed penalty.
method: Built CrystAF, an all-atom crystal flow-map generator.
Compared three physics-integration points: during training, after training, and at inference using the UMA interatomic potential.
Tested transfer of the same post-training strategy to Clari-M and MolCrystalFlow.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that post-training improves molecular validity and crystal packing, UMA relaxation slows generation by 6–26×, and the approach generalizes across multiple generator architectures.
watch_item: Inference-time relaxation can repair local clashes, but over-reliance on it may be expensive and cannot fully replace learning physically aligned structure priors.
paper_title: Where Should Physics Enter a Molecular Crystal Generator?
